title: Using AI to Foster Critical Thinking in the Classroom
author: Nick Potkalitsky, Chrissy Macso
summary: This guest-collaboration post pairs a framing introduction from Nick Potkalitsky with a seventh-grade ELA teacher's account of using ChatGPT as a thought partner in a novel unit on Klara and the Sun. Chrissy Macso describes moving from skepticism to adoption, pairing the novel with a persuasive essay unit and modelling prompt refinement on a classroom display. She reports benefits for students with writer's block and lively debate about whether artificial friends can feel empathy, while flagging the risk that students blur fiction and real AI capabilities. She also argues that middle schoolers will meet AI anyway, so instruction should come first in a supported setting. Potkalitsky closes by connecting Ishiguro's themes to the current moment. It is an enthusiastic practitioner report with limited evidence beyond anecdote.
points: Macso positions ChatGPT as a thought partner and models prompt revision live so that students see AI as a tool for refining arguments, not a source of answers.
Pairing a novel about artificial friends with a persuasive essay unit gave students a real ethical question to argue about AI.
Students concluded ChatGPT lacks the embodiment and sensory life of the fictional Klara, though some struggled to separate fiction from real AI capability.
The teacher argues that teaching AI to middle schoolers before they find it on their own builds digital literacy and ethical awareness.
The account is candid that the novelty carries privacy and bias concerns, to be met by conversation and experimentation rather than evidence.
quotes: To assist students in generating persuasive arguments, I introduced ChatGPT as a "thought partner." I explained to my students that AI could be used as a tool for critical thinking rather than a mere source of information.

This interactive process not only enhanced students' writing skills but also fostered a deeper understanding of the complexities surrounding AI. An added bonus I did not see coming is that it helped students who suffer from writer’s block. The information from ChatGPT gave them a starting point, and they immediately felt more at ease to get started on their outlines.

However, most students recognized that ChatGPT lacks the physical embodiment and sensory capabilities that were depicted in the novel with Klara. While ChatGPT could serve as a thought-provoking example of AI technology, the students ultimately concluded that it differs significantly from Klara and the AF world.

While exploring the themes of AI through Klara and the Sun alongside utilizing AI technology like ChatGPT in our classroom discussions, I observed some potential areas of concern that could impact consideration for future use. One misgiving that arose was the risk of blurring lines between fiction and reality for students.

Some may want to push back on introducing AI technology in the middle school years, but I disagree. Due to these formative years, students are naturally curious and technologically savvy, often exploring these tools independently or behind closed doors. By providing thoughtful and intentional instruction on AI in the classroom, educators can ensure that students develop a foundational understanding of these technologies within a controlled and supportive environment.

Ishiguro's work, known for its deep reflection on the evolving boundaries between human society and advancing technologies, is incredibly pertinent. His stories serve as nuanced warnings about the distribution of our choices, agency, and intelligence among artificial and automated systems.
